knowledge:
- key_parameters: zFPKM threshold=The reference recommends using zFPKM > -3 to select expressed/active genes. ;; input data=Works on gene-level FPKM or TPM data.
- alternatives: None mentioned, but the algorithm is based on the publication by Hart et al., 2013.
- when_to_use: Use when you have gene-level RNA-seq FPKM or TPM data and want a principled, validated threshold to identify detectably expressed (active) genes for downstream analysis.
- pitfalls: Does not appear to calibrate well for transcript-level data; it should only be used for gene-level data.

workflows.name: zfpkm_active_gene_filtering
workflows.intent: Perform zFPKM transformation on gene-level RNA-seq FPKM data, visualize the distribution fit, and filter for active genes.
input: SummarizedExperiment object containing FPKM and raw count assays, along with sample metadata.
workflows.stages: 1. Compute zFPKM scores using zFPKM() ;; 2. Plot the Gaussian fit using zFPKMPlot() ;; 3. Filter for active genes with median zFPKM > -3 within treatment groups.
workflows.code:
assay(se, "zfpkm") <- zFPKM(se)
zFPKMPlot(se)
activeGenes <- assay(se, "zfpkm") %>%
  mutate(gene=rownames(assay(se, "zfpkm"))) %>%
  gather(sample_id, zfpkm, -gene) %>%
  left_join(select(as.data.frame(colData(se)), sample_id, condition), by="sample_id") %>%
  group_by(gene, condition) %>%
  summarize(median_zfpkm=median(zfpkm)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(active=(median_zfpkm > -3)) %>%
  filter(active) %>%
  select(gene) %>%
  distinct()
